lessons: Never insert arbitrary pauses or interaction prompts like 'Pause and guess...', which lost 15.4% of viewers at 52% in the Maple Syrup video.
Avoid jumping directly into slow background setups after the hook; explaining sap composition lost 38.5% of viewers at 13% in the Maple Syrup video.
Keep verbal hooks tight; overly long descriptive hook sentences caused an immediate 22.4% viewer drop at 10% in the Cold Water video.
Focus on intrigue that naturally drives immediate rewatches at the start; videos with strong visual curiosity peaked above 1.0 retention at 10% (up to 1.178 in 'Why Onions Make You Cry').
Avoid closing with redundant side-questions near the end; asking another rhetorical question at 94% dropped 11.6% of viewers in the Cold Water video.
worst_moment_types: Artificial narrative pauses and prompts (e.g., 'Pause and guess...')
Slow, detailed scientific background setup immediately following the hook
Verbose, wordy hook lines that take too long to deliver the payoff
Tack-on rhetorical questions in the final seconds of the video
best_hook_types: Visual curiosity hooks that encourage immediate rewinds (>1.0 retention at 10%)
Concise problem statements that get directly to the core topic without verbal filler
